trabalhos.doutorado_desc: PhD candidate in Computer Science at the Federal University of Minas Gerais (UFMG), with emphasis on Distributed Systems. The research investigates Adaptive Security Orchestration at the Network Edge: an autonomous approach based on Multi-Agent Systems and Small Language Models (SLMs), combining cybersecurity, edge computing, and applied artificial intelligence.
trabalhos.doutorado_tema: Topic: Adaptive Security Orchestration at the Network Edge
trabalhos.gestao_desc: Works with management and technological innovation, leading digital transformation and the development of scalable, secure solutions aligned with strategic business goals.
trabalhos.ciberseguranca_desc: Former researcher in the field of Security Architecture, focused on the planning and development of Safety by Design (SbD) and Privacy by Design (PbD) systems. He carried out a project that involved static (SAST) and dynamic (DAST) vulnerability analysis in the systems of the Public Prosecutor's Office of Minas Gerais (MPMG) and the Integrated Security Office (GSI). Additionally, with an article published in the Integrated Software and Hardware Seminar (SEMISH) 2025.
trabalhos.ciberseguranca_desc2: See also an essay on "Quantum Computing and Cybersecurity: The Promising Future and Its Challenges" available below.
trabalhos.mineracao_desc: A project focused on discovering patterns in apartment rental data in the USA. Several data cleaning and analysis techniques were applied and discussed in the report available below.
trabalhos.analise_desc: Mapped the average prices of apartments in the U.S. and identified areas where high-priced apartments are concentrated.
trabalhos.itemsets_desc: We identified significant patterns among the amenities offered in apartments, revealing frequent and relevant associations between itemsets.
trabalhos.subgrupos_desc: We identified relevant subgroups for analysis, aiming to understand the relationship between certain offered amenities and the type of apartment and the region it is part of.
trabalhos.simplex_desc: Developed by George Dantzig in 1947, the Simplex algorithm is a powerful and efficient method for solving linear programming problems. This work was developed during the Operations Research course (DCC035), taught by Professor Cristiano Arbex Valle (PhD in Applied Mathematics). The project was implemented in Python and uses the extended LP model, providing optimality/infeasibility certificates. Thus, it can solve various LPs with great performance.
trabalhos.gps_desc: A GPS system was developed for the UFMG racing team’s car. This system used the following technologies: Arduino, C++, U-blox NEO-6M GPS, Google Colab, Python, Pandas, Folium, Plotly, and TinyGPS.
trabalhos.gps_desc2: The development was end-to-end, from assembling the components on Arduino to processing and analyzing the collected data. You can view the analyses and even test the code with other GPS data in the same U-blox format.
trabalhos.desenv_software_desc: Builds production products and systems, from cultural management and logistics platforms to digital publishing solutions such as an online store and library and a book layout studio. The work covers architecture, interface, and continuous delivery of software aligned with each business need.
trabalhos.ia_desc: Works as a developer at Radio Memory, focusing on neural network development and supporting AI innovations aimed at radiology solutions.
